note: Grounded in the real mechanism: a per-widget third-party setting `limited_field_widgets.limit_values` (integer, 0 = unlimited) stored on the form-display widget component of an UNLIMITED-cardinality field, plus an ItemCount validation constraint. Medium/hard cases create namespaced string fields (field_lfw_*) with cardinality -1 on node.article and read/write the limit_values setting on core.entity_form_display.node.article.default. Cleanup deletes only the field_lfw_* storages it created.

evals.prompt: I have a Drupal field with Unlimited cardinality but I want editors to add at most 3 values. Using the limited_field_widgets module, where and how do I set that cap? There is no admin settings page for the module.
evals.expected_output: On the bundle's Manage form display, open the field widget's gear and set 'Limit values' to 3. It is stored as third_party_settings.limited_field_widgets.limit_values on the widget component (and on the FieldConfig).

evals.prompt: On which fields does the limited_field_widgets 'Limit values' setting appear, and what does setting it to 0 mean?
evals.expected_output: The setting only appears for fields whose storage cardinality is Unlimited (CARDINALITY_UNLIMITED / -1). A value of 0 means unlimited (no cap; no ItemCount constraint is added).

evals.prompt: Besides hiding the 'Add another' button in the form, how does limited_field_widgets make sure the configured maximum is enforced even when an entity is saved programmatically?
evals.expected_output: hook_entity_bundle_field_info_alter() adds an 'ItemCount' validation constraint (max = limit) to the field, so validation fails when the value count exceeds the max — enforced on any save, not just the UI.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article content type has an unlimited field field_lfw_known whose widget uses limited_field_widgets to cap the number of values. Inspect the live default form display and tell me the maximum number of values allowed.

The Article content type has two unlimited fields, field_lfw_capped and field_lfw_free. One has a limited_field_widgets values cap set and the other does not. Inspect the live form display and state the value cap configured on field_lfw_capped.
evals.expected_output: field_lfw_capped is capped at 2 (limit_values = 2); field_lfw_free has limit_values = 0 (unlimited).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article content type has an unlimited field field_lfw_task with a string_textfield widget on the default form display. Using limited_field_widgets, configure that widget so editors can add at most 3 values. Apply the change to the live site.

On this Drupal site, the Article content type has an unlimited field field_lfw_single with a string_textfield widget on the default form display. Make it so an editor can enter only ONE value, using the limited_field_widgets module. Apply the change to the live site.
